If using the argument that "GIF" should be pronounced with a hard 'g' because "Graphics" is, it would follow that "JPEG" should be pronounced with an 'ph' (f) sound because "Photographic" is.

That would make sense if it was spelled jpheg, or if photographic was spelled potographic. Fact of the matter is the p is not pronounced like an f in either case. The combination of the p and the h is. Without the combination you do not have the f sound. If you could find me an instance of a p pronounced like an f then you might have an argument.

Maybe you're not getting the point or maybe I wasn't clear enough. Let me try to explain, and bear with me as I may explain things you already understand in the process.

People generally say "GIF" with a hard 'g' and not with a soft 'g' (like "jif"). Technically, the correct pronunciation is "jif" (per inventor and specification), but that's just not what people say. So basically, "jif" is the formal and "gif" is the colloquial. (Mind you, I'm fine with this.)

So the original video (and original gif post here "Its GIF not JIF") makes the argument that the correct pronunciation is "gif" because "Graphics" has a hard 'g' sound (note, it has nothing to do with the letter but with the sound). The argument is "supported" by changing a bunch of hard 'g' sounding words (not acronyms) to having the soft 'g' (j) sound.

People generally say "JPEG" as "jay-peg". JPEG has the P in it for Photographic, just as GIF has the G in it for Graphics. Photographic has an 'f' sound, just as Graphics has a hard 'g' sound. Therefore, the argument would extend to say JPEG must be pronounced with the 'f' sound, like "jay-feg", because Photographic has the same sound and is distinctively not Potographic.

So the { GIF <==> Graphics hard 'g' } argument is absurd. The same thing could be done with SCUBA. Even though it stands for Self Contained Underwater Breathing Apparatus people pronounce it "scoo-buh" not "scuh-baa." Or NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration - which is pronounced "naa-suh" and not "ne-saa."

Acronyms are supposed to be pronounced as the "word" they form and not based on the pronunciation of the elements. My attempt at "It's JPEG, not JPHEG!" was supposed to highlight the absurdity of the argument and the ridiculousness of trying to support it by arbitrarily changing word sounds. Unfortunately (for me), it's moot as people don't care.

The only valid argument for saying "GIF" instead of "JIF" is simply because it has become the accepted pronunciation, and "jif" has depreciated, so to speak.

I am saying the reasoning does not apply to both situations. The P is for photographic, but no matter what it stands for a singular P can not be pronounced as an F. A singular G on the other hand can be pronounced as a hard G or the soft J.

To apply it to our examples. If the words were not acronyms, JPEG would acceptable. JPHEG would not be. Because JPHEG would not be how you would pronounce it if it were not an acronym, it is not an acceptable pronunciation of it as an acronym. On the other hand GIF and JIF would both be acceptable pronunciations if the words were not acronyms. A G followed by a vowel is sometime pronounced as a J as in giraffe, or a G as in give. In SCUBA and NASA how you pronounce that word if it were not an acronym determines how you pronounce the word as an acronym.

TLDR: This reasoning does not apply to JPEG because in no circumstance would a singular P be pronounced as an F.

My TLDR is that it doesn't apply in either situation. I was using reductio ad absurdum to demonstrate it shouldn't apply to GIF.

In SCUBA and NASA how you pronounce that word if it were not an acronym determines how you pronounce the word as an acronym.

Yes... that's exactly what I was getting at. In fact, I said almost the exact same thing:

Acronyms are supposed to be pronounced as the "word" they form and not based on the pronunciation of the elements.

In English, the general rule (yes, I know there are exceptions) is that GIF be pronounced "jif" because of the "word" it forms, similar to the way SCUBA and NASA are pronounced. It has nothing to do with the elements of the acronym. Hence, any emphasis on "Graphics" for pronunciation is illogical.

However the word GIF could be pronounced either way, this is the reason we defer to the word the G represents. We do not with JPEG because it is not necessary. There is a difference there. The general rule in english does not say how GIF should be pronounced. It is like gaff, give, goad, get? Or is it like germ, giant, gym?

Because it is not clear in the way SCUBA and NASA are, we refer to the word it represents.
